labs.title: Pace, Learn budget and answer changes
steps: Signal sprint: 15 stems from the four domain banks, 45 seconds each, write only the signal phrase.
Ten-item set at the PA2 first-pass rate (1.7 minutes) with a visible clock and no Learn.
Write the three rules on a card: Learn only for a fact once the item is solved (2 min, 6 per form); change an answer only for a new fact or a misread stem; flag and move on after twice the rate.
labs.exit: Ten items in at most 17 minutes, no Learn, no answer changed without a written reason.

labs.title: Bulk writes that isolate bad rows
steps: Fill the write-pattern table for standard and elastic tables: CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple/UpsertMultiple, ExecuteMultiple with ContinueOnError, ExecuteTransaction, $batch change sets.
Run lesson 78's bulk sample against the fake service with one invalid row in a batch of 1,000 and compare the two strategies' saved counts.
Rewrite PA-38's solution so it meets every part of the goal.
labs.exit: Explain closed-book what one bad row does to UpsertMultiple on a standard table, to ExecuteMultiple with ContinueOnError and to CreateMultiple on an elastic table.

labs.title: Identity gates: token, user, role, resource
steps: Draw the four gates for an app-only call: Entra token, application user in the environment, security role privileges, Azure role on an Azure resource.
Sort eight Cedar error messages to the gate that produced them.
For each, write the one change that opens that gate and nothing else.
labs.exit: Name the gate and the least-privilege fix for "missing prvWriteIncident", "not a user of the organization", AADSTS700016 and a 403 from Key Vault.

labs.title: Alert latency budget
steps: Write the latency of each signal source: Monitor alert rules (24-hour evaluation), admin export to Application Insights (up to a day), own telemetry (minutes), per-item notification (immediate).
Write the KQL and alert settings for PA-42's requirement 4 and compare with the published solution.
Classify five Cedar monitoring requirements by the number in each.
labs.exit: For any requirement with a time limit, name the fastest suitable source and why each slower one fails.

labs.title: Lookup filters and CSP directives
steps: Write the OnLoad handler that adds one PreSearch filter reading the current service line (PA-13), and say why addPreSearch in OnChange stacks filters.
Draw the parent and child frames for the Dispatch Planner: who embeds whom, and which directive governs each arrow.
Answer four directive questions with the frame drawing only.
labs.exit: Say which directive allows the app to be embedded and which allows the app to embed, with one Cedar example of each, without notes.

labs.title: Long-running custom API calls
steps: Send cedar_RecalculateContracts with Prefer: respond-async in Cedar-Test (or read the recorded responses in the lesson) and follow the Location URL.
Fill the table: asynchronous step versus background operation (who waits, what returns, time limit, preview status).
labs.exit: Explain why an asynchronous step can't free a caller that needs a result, and what Prefer: respond-async changes and doesn't change.

labs.title: Code app flows and connector metadata
steps: List which flows a code app can call and add one with pa app list-flows and pa app add flow (or read the commands in the lesson).
Write the x-ms-dynamic-values block for PA-32 and an enum for a fixed list; mark which values change.
labs.exit: For a parameter list, decide enum or x-ms-dynamic-values from how often the values change, and name the four dynamic-values properties.

labs.title: Choosing the automation host
steps: Fill the decision table: Power Automate cloud flow, agent flow, Copilot Studio workflow, classic workflow (who calls it, billing, when to use).
Classify six Cedar automation requests.
labs.exit: Say in one sentence each when an agent flow is right and when a cloud flow is right, with the capacity each consumes.

labs.title: Calibration: re-rate Build closed-book
steps: List Build ratings of 2 or 3 whose evidence is older than 1 December (remediation.mjs --stale).
For each, recall the rule card closed-book and explain it aloud in under two minutes.
Recalled: rating 2 with dated evidence (a recall proves 2, not 3). Not recalled: rating 1.
labs.exit: Every stale Build rating has evidence dated after 1 December, and C-73 Build readiness is recomputed from it.

labs.title: Plug-in registration and performance
steps: Order the six optimisation moves (don't run, run later, read less, write less, hold locks briefly, measure) and match each to a registration setting or code change.
For a step that needs a region code and an API key, say where each value lives and which travels with the solution.
labs.exit: Say closed-book what filtering attributes, images, unsecure configuration, secure configuration and managed identity for plug-ins each do, and which are exported.

labs.title: Connector functions and custom code
steps: Draw the call from a flow through the connector and API Management to the function, and mark where the user's identity is checked.
List the custom code limits (time, size, one script, no gateway, no logging) and what a policy template can and can't do.
labs.exit: Explain why a function key can't tell the function who the user is, and what App Service authentication adds, without notes.

labs.title: Solution layers and code app data
steps: Draw the layer stack of a form with an active unmanaged layer and say what publishing, update, upgrade and removing the active layer each change.
Write the update call for one changed column and the getMetadata call for a display name, with caching.
labs.exit: Say which layer wins and how to remove it, and why an update sends only changed columns, without notes.
